explanation: The name means 'ox-head'. When the horse died in 326 BC, in modern Pakistan, Alexander founded a city nearby and named it Bucephala. Incitatus was Caligula's horse, and Marengo was Napoleon's.

claims.text: Alexander the Great's best-known horse was Bucephalus.
Incitatus was the emperor Caligula's horse, Marengo was Napoleon's and Copenhagen was the Duke of Wellington's.
The name Bucephalus means 'ox-head' in Greek.
Bucephalus died in 326 BC, around the time of the Battle of the Hydaspes, in what is modern Pakistan.
Alexander founded a city named Bucephala in the horse's honour.
